subject: How to alter the order of the keys in a legend?

messages.author: 259bffad7213efef
messages.subject: How to alter the order of the keys in a legend?
parts:
Hi,

How can I alter the order of the keys in a legend of a stacked
barchart? I've tried to use "Branche" as a ordered factor, but it
doesn't work:

factor(c(rep("Textil",6),rep("Metall/Maschinen",6),rep("Uhren",6),rep
("Chemie/Pharmazie",6),rep("Nahrungsmittel",6),rep("Andere",6)),
ordered=TRUE)

With this factor it works, but it isn't very elegant:

factor(c(rep("a_Textil",6),rep("b_Metall/Maschinen",6),rep("c_Uhren",
6),rep("d_Chemie/Pharmazie",6),rep("e_Nahrungsmittel",6),rep
("f_Andere",6)), ordered=TRUE)

My barchart:
q<-ggplot(k, aes(x=Jahr, y=Export, fill=Branche))
r<- q + layer(
geom="bar",
position="stack",
stat_params = list(binwidth = 1)
)
r

Thanks a lot.
Ruedi

messages.subject: Re: How to alter the order of the keys in a legend?
parts:
I have a related question:

It seems that the default order of keys in legend is opposite of the order in stacking bars, for example:
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/position_stack.html
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/position_fill.html

In my opinion it will be easier to look up keys if they are in the same order.

Regards,
Xie Chao

messages.subject: Re: How to alter the order of the keys in a legend?
parts:
Thanks to Hadley, thanks to Xie Chao!
At last, I've found a solution by xavier.chardon at rennes.inra.fr
that works.
The example with the data I've sent yesterday follows.
Kind regards
Ruedi

#package
library(ggplot2)

#read data
zwila<-data.frame(read.table("data.txt"
, header=TRUE, sep="", na.strings="NA", dec=".", strip.white=TRUE))
colnames(zwila)<-c("Jahr", "Branche", "Export")


#theme

ep_theme <- theme_update(
axis.text.x = theme_text( colour='grey50'),
axis.text.y = theme_text(hjust=1, colour='grey50'),
panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour='grey80'),
panel.grid.minor = theme_line(colour='grey80'),

axis.ticks = theme_blank(),
legend.position =c(0.30,0.79))



#Solution of xavier.chardon at rennes.inra.fr
#res$f1 <- factor(res$f1, levels = unique(res$f1) )
#with f1 sorted in the order you want it to appear.

zwila$Branche <- factor(zwila$Branche, levels = unique(zwila
$Branche))

q<-ggplot(zwila, aes(x=Jahr, y=Export, fill=Branche))

r<- q + layer(
geom="bar",
position="stack",
stat_params = list(binwidth = 1)
)
r
